liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Alabama Getaway** (2 reviews): The crowd was insane during the opening song, with Phil thumping away energetically; Blown lyrics occurred right off the bat in the opening song and Promised Land [11][13]
- **Promised Land** (1 review): Bob forgets words and sings off key at times in this track [15]
- **Far From Me** (1 review): This performance is a historic event, though shaky with Bret forgetting to come in [15]
- **Tennessee Jed** (1 review): Jerry truncated the jam section in the middle, resulting in the shortest version ever [13]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Jerry and Bob made mistakes but were on fire during this extended jam [11]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Jerry's solo is described as cheesy and meandering, unlike the Las Vegas 83 version [18]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review): The performance features a weird tempo, though Jerry's playing is described as nice [9]
- **Black Peter** (1 review): The transition into Sugar Magnolia and U.S. Blues is considered the standout moment [8]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-03-30.mtx.motb.96455.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 170 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [1]
- **gd1980-03-30.fob.glassberg.motb-0082.96015.flac24**: source not stated; 20 songs; 168 min [2]. Said about its sound: All circulating sources have cuts at the end of Saint of Circumstance [2]
- **gd1980-03-30.sbd.miller.92666.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 148 min; rated 3.5/5 by 4 [4]
- **gd80-03-30.sbd.miller.27752.sbeok.flacf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 151 min; rated 3.56/5 by 9 [5]. Said about its sound: The recording is clear but suffers from weak volume throughout the performance [7]
- **gd80-03-30.glassberg.barbella.4740.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 161 min; rated 3.62/5 by 13 [6]. Said about its sound: Brent's synth sounded like a little toy piano during the Go to Heaven period [14]

## Around the show

- John Belushi sang on the encore of U.S. Blues, which the reviewer found cool [10]
- Tickets were hard to get for the small 1500-seat venue, unlike Radio City later [11]
- The reviewer was unaware of John Belushi's presence, having attended the next day instead [12]
- John Belushi appeared on stage during the encore, singing backup on U.S. Blues [14]
- John Belushi provided vocals and performed cartwheels during U.S. Blues [4]
- John Belushi joined on vocals and did cartwheels during Sugar Magnolia [5]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-03-30.mtx.motb.96455.flac16**: transferred by Derek McCabe; source: MTX: AUD(96014) and SBD(92666) [1]
- **gd1980-03-30.fob.glassberg.motb-0082.96015.flac24**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by Adam Egert and Derek McCabe; source: 2 x Nakamichi CM700 => Sony TC-D5M >> MAC [2]
- **gd1980-03-30.sbd.miller.92666.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Dat (44.1k) [4]. Also: Nakamichi 700 to Cassette Master to Dat to CD, remastered from shnid 27752 [4]
- **gd80-03-30.sbd.miller.27752.sbeok.flacf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard patched with Audience [5]
- **gd80-03-30.glassberg.barbella.4740.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Barry G.; source: Audience: Nakamichi 700's [6]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Capitol Theatre - March 30, 1980](https://www.dead.net/show/march-30-1980) [20]
